topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and frames the upcoming material on the complement system.

topics.label: Fundamentals, nomenclature, and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental architecture, naming conventions, and central importance of C3 cleavage in complement function.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct upstream pathways and convertase mechanisms that drive complement activation toward a trigger threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream processes through which activated complement destroys pathogens and mediates inflammation.

topics.label: Complement regulation and host protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how host cells use specialized regulatory proteins to prevent accidental complement activation on self-tissues.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how specific defects across different complement components and regulators produce distinct clinical pathologies.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the evolutionary strategies used by pathogens to inhibit or bypass complement-mediated clearance.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the discussion of complement and previews the next lecture on the adaptive immune system.
